title: Candidate silver TTM Ce and G digitized from Lin et al. (2008), Fig. 2(c,d)
citation: Z. Lin, L. V. Zhigilei, and V. Celli, Phys. Rev. B 77, 075133 (2008), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevB.77.075133

digitization.estimated_graph_reading_uncertainty: approximately 5% for plotted portions; digitization and model uncertainty are not included
digitization.Ce_low_temperature_rule: For Te<=5000 K, use the paper's quoted experimental gamma_exp=63.3 J m^-3 K^-2 multiplied by Te. The text says the plotted DOS result follows the low-Te linear form below several thousand kelvin; above 5000 K use the digitized Fig. 2(c) solid curve.
digitization.G_low_temperature_rule: Fig. 2(d) solid curve is approximately on a 0.25e17 W m^-3 K^-1 low-Te plateau. Hold this plotted plateau through 5000 K, then bridge linearly to the curve-tracing seed at 6607 K because the low-T trace overlaps experimental reference lines. Above the seed use traced Fig. 2(d).
digitization.caveat: These are extracted candidate curves, not original raw author tables. In particular the low-temperature G plateau and 5000–6607 K bridge are explicit graph-based approximations.
